title: Example only: cross-domain spectral analogy

analogy.target_feature: an approximately linear squared excitation spectrum
analogy.mapping: Map excitation number to radial mode number and the observed slope to an effective soft-wall scale.
analogy.known_breakdown: A matching spectral slope alone does not establish a holographic mechanism, a local five-dimensional dual, or matching dynamics.

hypothesis_statement: A target system with a robust linear squared excitation spectrum may admit a useful soft-wall-inspired reduced description over a specified finite regime.
mechanism: An effective one-dimensional fluctuation operator with harmonic infrared growth could generate approximately equally spaced squared eigenvalues without implying a fundamental gravity dual.
assumptions: The target spectrum and uncertainties are independently established.
The proposed mode identification is fixed before fitting.
A simpler non-holographic baseline is included.

predictions.statement: After fixing one overall scale, held-out squared excitation levels follow an approximately constant spacing within a preregistered tolerance.
predictions.observable: successive differences of squared excitation energies
predictions.regime: the finite excitation range declared before testing

falsification_tests.test: Fit the scale on a training subset and compare held-out levels against both the soft-wall pattern and a simpler baseline.
falsification_tests.failure_condition: Reject the proposal if it does not outperform the baseline within the preregistered uncertainty and complexity penalty.

prior_work.summary: This file demonstrates the schema only; no target system or novelty claim has been selected.

claims.statement: The proposed cross-domain mapping could be predictive after its scale is fixed.
claims.evidence: No target-system evidence yet; this is a schema example awaiting prior-work and baseline tests.

risks: Pattern matching may be mistaken for a dynamical explanation.
Flexible mode assignments may make the proposal unfalsifiable.
Existing non-holographic models may already explain the same spectrum.

required_evidence: A fixed target system and mode dictionary
A preregistered comparison with a simpler baseline
A reproducible calculation with uncertainty propagation
